doc: LEADERBOARD_PRD.md §3, §4, §6 — one entry per eval set. The site merges them into one table with labeled column groups; ranks stay within an eval set and are never mixed. `frozen` hashes were stamped at M4 (2026-08-27); each board's `frozen_note` says exactly what artifact its hashes digest. A board whose hashes are still TODO refuses every `add`. `pending` lists methods whose results are still computing; `build` drops an entry once a row for that method is stamped.

main.label: Full genome
main.subtitle: 23 chromosomes
main.rows_note: CANDI versions, retrained rivals, naive baselines.
main.eli5: The same training-to-validation pairs of a cell type the method already saw, scored on every chromosome in the store. This is missing-mark transfer, not an unseen-cell-type test. Methods that train on every genomic position are still in-sample here, so this column is not a standalone head-to-head.

frozen.frozen_note: store hash = sha256 of fir:/project/def-maxwl/mforooz/CANDI_STORE/eic/manifest.json, read on Fir 2026-08-27 — the manifest path every stamped row's score provenance names; regime hash = sha256 of the tracked configs/regime.eic_val.json (last changed at t31), verified byte-identical to the copies in the t50/t51/t52 Fir checkouts on 2026-08-27.

caveats: CANDI trained on chromosome-19 positions only, so on this board CANDI is in-sample on chr19 and held-out on the other 22.
Methods that train on every genomic position (Avocado, ChromImpute) are in-sample everywhere. No choice of eval chromosome removes this; it is disclosed on every row.

reader_badges.label: In-sample for position-trained methods
reader_badges.eli5: Avocado and ChromImpute train on every genomic position, so this column is not a standalone head-to-head. CANDI trained on chromosome 19 only. Internal code: P2 / main board, position transductivity.

reader_badges.label: Same cell type, held-out experiment
reader_badges.eli5: Each score is a mark the validation experiment has and the paired training experiment of that same cell type lacks. The method has seen the type. Blind-test pairs (regime.eic_test) are not this board. Internal code: eic_val eval_pairs.

pending.note: mainline (chr19 recipe) training on Fir; genome-wide queued (count+signal+peak)

dev.label: Chromosome 21
dev.subtitle: development set
dev.rows_note: The fast column new CANDI versions hit first; same methods as the full-genome column.
dev.eli5: A fast check on one chromosome, using the same training-to-validation pairs of a seen cell type. This is missing-mark transfer, not an unseen-cell-type test. Numbers here select what is worth scoring on the whole genome; they are not the headline result.

frozen.frozen_note: Same store and regime as the full-genome column — two protocols over one eval set. See that column's frozen_note for what each hash digests.

caveats: Development column — chromosome 21 only. Numbers here select what goes to the full-genome column; they are not the headline result.
CANDI trained on chromosome 19, so it is held-out on chromosome 21; methods that train on every position are in-sample here too.

reader_badges.label: Same cell type, held-out experiment
reader_badges.eli5: Each score is a mark the validation experiment has and the paired training experiment of that same cell type lacks. The method has seen the type. Blind-test pairs (regime.eic_test) are not this board. Internal code: eic_val eval_pairs.

pending.note: mainline (chr19 recipe) training on Fir; genome-wide queued (count+signal+peak)

entrants.label: 2019 challenge
entrants.subtitle: blind test
entrants.rows_note: The 23 ENCODE Imputation Challenge submissions, plus CANDI and baselines when they land.
entrants.eli5: The original 2019 challenge's hidden test tracks. This is a different truth signal from the other two columns — a number here cannot be compared to a number there.

frozen.frozen_note: The 2019 challenge has no store manifest and no regime json, so this column pins different artifacts: store hash = sha256 of cruxvault/results/t54/submissions_survey.json (the Synapse manifest — every scored prediction file with its size and md5), regime hash = sha256 of cruxvault/results/t54/placement.json (the ruled placement artifact every entrant row is extracted from; `add --placement-method` verifies the file it reads digests to exactly this).

caveats: The 2019 challenge used a different truth signal than the other two columns. Scores never translate between them (measured 12–66% per-experiment error for that move).
DNase-seq is left out of every 2019-challenge row: in the other two columns it is read-depth normalized signal, a different physical quantity.
Entrant rows are the 2019 submissions as frozen, not retrained; CUImpute1, CUWA and ICU submitted identical predictions and count once, not three times.

reader_badges.label: DNase-seq excluded
reader_badges.eli5: In the other two columns, DNase-seq is a different physical quantity (read-depth normalized signal), so it is left out here. Internal code: B3.
